sourcedFrom: Colt MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols Safety and Instruction Manual — MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols (1996)
cleanIntro: Colt's own field strip for the Combat Commander, then the cleaning it calls for. The Commander strips exactly as the Government Model does in Colt's own grouping; every step carries the manual's words and the page they sit on.

steps.title: Catch the magazine as it drops
steps.action: Put a hand under the magazine so it cannot fall, then press the magazine catch to release and eject it.
steps.prose: A magazine dropped onto concrete is a bent feed lip and a gun that stops working. Catch it.
steps.quote: Place hand under magazine to prevent it from falling and press magazine catch to release and eject magazine.
steps.cite: Colt MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols Safety and Instruction Manual — MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols — UNLOADING — To Unload, step 2, p.27
steps.warn: ALWAYS UNLOAD YOUR PISTOL IMMEDIATELY AFTER USE AND BEFORE CLEANING AND STORAGE to minimize the risk of accidental

steps.title: Rack the chambered round out
steps.action: Using the serrated finger grips, pull the slide sharply rearward to extract and eject the round in the chamber.
steps.prose: Sharply, not gently. A slow pull is how a live round gets left sitting half out of the chamber.
steps.caution: Keep your hands clear of the ejection port to allow round to eject without obstruction.
steps.quote: Using serrated finger grips pull slide sharply rearward to extract and eject a round from the chamber.
steps.cite: Colt MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols Safety and Instruction Manual — MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols — UNLOADING — To Unload, step 3, p.27

steps.title: Look into the chamber, then lower the hammer
steps.action: Pull the slide back slightly and look into the chamber to be sure it is empty, then let the slide return forward on the empty chamber and squeeze the trigger to lower the hammer, keeping the muzzle in a safe direction throughout.
steps.prose: Look — do not feel, and do not trust the extractor. The hammer only comes down after your own eyes have confirmed the chamber.
steps.quote: Pull slide back slightly and LOOK IN CHAMBER TO ENSURE
steps.cite: Colt MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols Safety and Instruction Manual — MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols — LOADING, step 3, p.24 (hammer lowered per UNLOADING step 5, p.28)

steps.title: Empty the magazine as well
steps.action: Slide the remaining live rounds forward out of the magazine, then collect them for safe storage.
steps.prose: Forward over the feed lips, one at a time. A cleared pistol beside a loaded magazine is not a cleared pistol.
steps.quote: Remove remaining live rounds by sliding them forward out of the magazine.
steps.cite: Colt MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols Safety and Instruction Manual — MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols — UNLOADING — To Unload, step 6, p.28

steps.title: The Commanders strip as group A, alongside the Government Model
steps.action: Colt splits its stripping instructions three ways, and both Commanders sit in group A with the Government Model, Delta Elite, Combat Elite, Combat Target and the M1991A1 models. Group B is the Officer's ACP and Compact; group C is the Colt Defender. Everything below is the group-A procedure.
steps.prose: The Combat Commander differs from the Government Model in size, weight and barrel configuration — a shorter slide and barrel over the same frame — and none of that changes the order the parts come off in.
steps.quote: The Combat Commander and Commander Model (Lightweight) semi-automatic pistols are identical in appearance and function.
steps.cite: Colt MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols Safety and Instruction Manual — MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols — SECTION 2 MAIN FEATURES, p.4

steps.title: Magazine out, pistol proven empty
steps.action: Before the strip begins, confirm again that the magazine is out and the pistol is not loaded, and be sure you have read the manual's safety instructions.
steps.prose: Colt restates the clearing at the head of its own stripping section rather than assuming you did it. Do it again anyway.
steps.quote: Ensure magazine is removed and pistol is NOT loaded.
steps.cite: Colt MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols Safety and Instruction Manual — MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols — STRIPPING FOR CLEANING, step 1, p.34
steps.warn: ENSURE THAT MAGAZINE IS REMOVED AND THE PISTOL IS NOT LOADED BEFORE STRIPPING AND CLEANING, so that pistol will not fire.

steps.title: Stand it on its butt, muzzle up
steps.action: With the muzzle pointing upward, rest the pistol on the heel of the butt and the grip safety on a table or bench.
steps.prose: This is not fussiness. The recoil spring plug is about to be released under compression, and standing the gun up puts your body out of its line.
steps.caution: Wear safety glasses — the springs are strong and could fly out and injure or even blind somebody if they are not handled with care.
steps.quote: With muzzle pointing upward, rest pistol on heel of butt and "grip safety" on a table or bench.
steps.cite: Colt MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols Safety and Instruction Manual — MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols — STRIPPING FOR CLEANING, step 2, p.35

steps.title: Free the plug: press down and turn the bushing
steps.action: Push the slide back about a quarter inch, press down on the recoil spring plug just below the muzzle and at the same time rotate the barrel bushing clockwise about a quarter turn, using a bushing wrench if you need one.
steps.prose: Both hands are busy at once: down on the plug, round on the bushing. Let go of the plug at this point and it leaves the gun at speed.
steps.quote: Push slide back about 1/4 inch, press down on recoil spring plug (located just below muzzle) and at same time rotate barrel bushing clockwise about 1/4 turn, using barrel bushing wrench if necessary; this will free plug and recoil spring.
steps.cite: Colt MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols Safety and Instruction Manual — MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols — STRIPPING FOR CLEANING, step 3 (A), p.35

steps.title: Let the plug and spring out under control
steps.action: Keep pressure on the plug so the spring cannot eject it, and allow plug and spring to extend gradually out of the slide. Then rotate the plug counterclockwise and take it off the spring.
steps.prose: Gradually is the operative word. The spring has an inch of travel it wants to use all at once.
steps.caution: Rotate plug counterclockwise and remove from spring.
steps.quote: Keep pressure on plug to prevent it being ejected by the spring, then allow plug and spring to gradually extend out of the slide.
steps.cite: Colt MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols Safety and Instruction Manual — MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols — STRIPPING FOR CLEANING, step 3 (A), p.35

steps.title: Cock the hammer
steps.action: Pull back on the hammer spur until the hammer is cocked.
steps.prose: The slide will not come off over a down hammer. This is the step people skip and then blame on a tight gun.
steps.quote: Cock hammer by pulling back on hammer spur.
steps.cite: Colt MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols Safety and Instruction Manual — MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols — STRIPPING FOR CLEANING, step 4, p.36

steps.title: Line up the disassembly notch and push the pin through
steps.action: Pull the slide to the rear until the lug on the slide stop sits opposite the disassembly notch, then push the rounded end of the slide stop pin — on the right of the receiver — inward and through the receiver to disengage it from the slide.
steps.prose: The notch is a shallow half-moon in the slide rail; if the pin will not move, the notch is not lined up. Push, do not lever.
steps.quote: Pull slide to rear until lug on slide stop is opposite disassembly notch
steps.cite: Colt MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols Safety and Instruction Manual — MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols — STRIPPING FOR CLEANING, step 5, p.36

steps.title: Lift the slide stop out
steps.action: Take the slide stop out of the receiver.
steps.prose: It lifts straight out on the left once the pin is clear. Put it somewhere it cannot roll off the bench.
steps.cite: Colt MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols Safety and Instruction Manual — MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols — STRIPPING FOR CLEANING, step 6, p.37

steps.title: Slide forward off the receiver
steps.action: Push the slide forward and off the front of the receiver.
steps.prose: Straight forward. Nothing needs to be held back once the slide stop is out.
steps.quote: Push slide forward off the receiver.
steps.cite: Colt MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols Safety and Instruction Manual — MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols — STRIPPING FOR CLEANING, step 7, p.37

steps.title: Recoil spring and guide out the back of the slide
steps.action: Lift the recoil spring and its guide and draw them rearward out of the slide.
steps.prose: Rearward, the way they went in. Pulling them out the muzzle end fights the guide's arched foot.
steps.quote: Lift recoil springs and guide and pull them rearward out of slide.
steps.cite: Colt MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols Safety and Instruction Manual — MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols — STRIPPING FOR CLEANING, step 8 (A & B), p.37

steps.title: Bushing off, then barrel out through the front
steps.action: Turn the barrel bushing counterclockwise, push barrel and bushing forward until the bushing is clear of the slide and take the bushing off the barrel. Then push the barrel link forward and remove the barrel from the slide.
steps.prose: The link has to be forward or the barrel lug will not clear its seat — Colt gives that its own figure for a reason.
steps.quote: Push link forward and remove barrel from slide.
steps.cite: Colt MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols Safety and Instruction Manual — MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols — STRIPPING FOR CLEANING, steps 9 and 10, p.37

steps.title: Field strip complete — and that is the limit
steps.action: Receiver, slide, barrel, barrel bushing, recoil spring, spring guide, recoil spring plug, slide stop and magazine. Colt prints the bound on the same page: do not strip the pistol further, and do not remove or alter parts, particularly safety parts.
steps.prose: Anything past this line is a gunsmith's job by the manufacturer's own instruction, not a matter of confidence.
steps.quote: Do not strip your pistol further than previously described. Do not remove or alter parts, particularly safety parts.
steps.cite: Colt MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols Safety and Instruction Manual — MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols — STRIPPING FOR CLEANING — IMPORTANT, p.38
steps.warn: NEVER DRY FIRE THE PISTOL WHEN THE SLIDE IS REMOVED FROM THE RECEIVER, and do not after parts as the level of safety could be reduced.

deepAbsentReason: Colt bounds this book on the last page of its stripping section: "Do not strip your pistol further than previously described. Do not remove or alter parts, particularly safety parts." (p.38), and directs anything beyond it to "Service and Repair". The only further procedure the manual publishes is magazine disassembly (pp.48–50), which is a magazine job and is carried in the cleaning list below. So this listing has NO deep clean — the manual documents no procedure past the field strip, and inventing one is not an option.

cleaning.name: BARREL AND CHAMBER
tasks: Clean from the breech end forward — Colt warns that contact between cleaning rod and muzzle wears the crown and reduces accuracy
Attach a cotton flannel patch to the rod, insert it in the breech and pass rod and patch down through the barrel, changing patches until the last one comes out clean

If the bore is still dirty after firing, run a brass wire bristle brush wet with gun cleaning solution the full length before reversing direction — change direction with the brush inside and it will stick
Finish with a lightly oil-moistened patch through the bore, leaving a thin film; pass a dry patch through if the pistol is going back into use rather than storage

cleaning.name: BREECH FACE AND SLIDE
tasks: Clean the rear face of the barrel and the face of the slide with a small toothbrush
Wipe the rails inside the slide and the rails on the receiver with a lightly oiled patch
Put one small drop of oil in each of the locking grooves in the slide
Put one small drop of oil on the hammer pivot pin, the barrel link pin and the sear pivot pin — slide movement distributes the rest

cleaning.name: WIPE DOWN
tasks: Check no flannel or brush bristles have lodged anywhere in the pistol
Wipe every metal surface you can reach with a flannel patch lightly moistened with gun oil, including the barrel bushing area
After reassembly, wipe the external surfaces again to remove fingerprints — finger moisture left behind starts corrosion
Remove gun cleaning solution and oil from the stocks

cleaning.name: MAGAZINE
tasks: Clean the magazine whenever the pistol is cleaned
Remove the follower and spring and clean all components, taking care to remove carbon deposits from the magazine lips and the follower
Wipe the components with a lightly oiled cloth and reassemble
Note which way yours comes apart: 10mm and .40 S&W magazines are disassembled from the bottom, most other calibres from the top

cleaning.name: HOW OFTEN
tasks: Clean as soon after firing as possible — the job is easier and there is less chance for corrosion to start
Unfired, clean it once or twice a year in a temperate climate, or as often as once a month in a tropical one
If you carry it loaded, unload it and clean it at least once a month; if it gets wet, clean it as soon as possible
Below freezing, avoid oil and apply a dry lubricant sparingly instead

reassembly: With the slide upside down and the barrel link forward, assemble the barrel into the slide.
Place the barrel bushing over the muzzle and into the slide until it is flush with the face of the slide, then turn the bushing clockwise as far as it will go.

Put the recoil spring guide into the spring so the closed end of the spring is against the collar of the guide, push the open end of the spring through the slide from the rear, and position the arched part of the guide over the outside of the barrel.
Cock the hammer, check the plunger lever on top of the receiver is down (forward), and tip the receiver forward to keep it down as you run the slide onto the receiver.

Look through the slide stop hole and move the slide until the hole in the barrel link lines up with it, insert the slide stop until it is almost home, then push the slide rearward until the disassembly notch lines up and press the slide stop fully in against its plunger.

Rest the pistol on the bench muzzle up, push the slide back about a quarter inch, press the recoil spring plug down until it is fully home, and rotate the barrel bushing so its arched part straddles the plug and locks it in place.
fncheck: Run Colt's own post-assembly check (p.46): remove the magazine, pull the slide fully back and let it go — it should fly forward and close on the empty chamber with the hammer staying cocked. Push the safety up and squeeze the trigger; the hammer should stay cocked. Push the safety down and squeeze; the hammer should fall. Then insert an empty magazine, pull the slide back and let go — it should NOT fly forward — and look into the ejection port to be sure the firing pin is not sticking through the breech face. If the firing pin is protruding, or the pistol discharges when you close the slide, do not use it: return it to Colt.
